reason: Considered HOLD after limited web research (three searches; none found news dated 11-12 or 11-13 for my names, so the most recent thing I could verify is from 11-11). The book is +7.43% vs SPY +1.74% with a -4.49% max drawdown, and every leg is well inside its stop (worst is XOM at -4.3% against a -15% stop). Healthcare: Cigna beat Q3 on Nov 5 and raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $30.60. It is buying back stock and trades at about 10x guided EPS. The stock fell after the report on Express Scripts margin pressure and the planned 2027 move away from rebates, but it recovered to about $303 by Nov 10 and marks $297. That is the kind of reset in a cheap cash returner this mandate is meant to own, so it is not a reason to sell. CVS, PFE and BMY: I found no new thesis-breaking items. The PBM and drug-pricing probe headlines are long-running, and the low multiples already price them in. Energy: Brent fell sharply from about $118 in late October to a 10-week low near $91.50 on Nov 10, after Hormuz flows and OPEC output rose. It rebounded to about $92.50 on Nov 11 when renewed Hormuz shipping attacks dented peace hopes. CVX and XOM fell only 2-4% through that roughly 20% crude drawdown. They remain FCF-positive at $90 Brent, and the 19% stub is a deliberate hedge against the Hormuz tail risk, which is still live, so trimming it after the crude flush would mean selling the hedge at the wrong moment. Citi is +2.5% with its bank-rerating thesis intact. Nothing has changed enough to justify paying churn costs, so I keep the 25% cash at 4% APY as dry powder.
